topic: Sharp generated-donor-proxy minimax frontier for realized-path causal buy-and-hold level wealth. Fix H, proxy dimension p and finitely many cohorts; observe N donor scores and n_s replicated untreated wealth blocks across T pre-event windows, with conditional cross-unit independence, geometric temporal beta-mixing, bounded wealth, stable Holder(lambda) proxy-coordinate regressions, interior event-path overlap, limited anticipation and no spillovers. Use the full uniformly elliptic conditional covariance of the stacked donor-error path. At each realized event path impose a two-sided covariance-standardized local modulus with kappa=min(lambda,1). Determine sharp conditional MSE and uniformly honest expected-length rates across arbitrary N,T,n_s growth, the exact oracle/generated-proxy phase diagram, an attaining replicated-donor cross-fitted local-polynomial or tensor-sieve estimator with calendar-block inference, and matching Le Cam/Assouad bounds. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: In the scalar H=0, one-cohort Gaussian-donor subexperiment, event locations O(N^-1/2) apart have bounded KL; affine or asymmetric-cusp regressions satisfying the corrected modulus separate targets by O(N^-kappa/2), yielding MSE N^-kappa and honest-length N^-kappa/2 lower bounds, matched by known-regression plug-in. Checks excluded constant-regression, noiseless temporal-contrast, cohort-cancellation, and identified prior-art collisions; the combined four-term rate remains heuristic and unproved. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove one feasible estimator and conditionally honest interval attain the maximum of treated-mean noise, replicated-response smoothing, random-design spacing, and proxy-modulus terms under unknown heteroscedastic donor laws and overlapping beta-mixing windows, with matching lower bounds in every relative-growth regime and no extra deconvolution or logarithmic phase. EARLY KILL TEST: In scalar iid H=0 with lambda=kappa<=1, bounded responses, T latent design points, n response replicates, and N donor replicates, prove MSE max{n^-1,(Tn)^(-2lambda/(2lambda+1)),T^(-2lambda),N^-lambda} and the square-root honest-length rate; pivot if noisy training covariates force any larger term.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether the scalar iid generated-donor experiment has sharp MSE max{n^-1,(Tn)^(-2lambda/(2lambda+1)),T^(-2lambda),N^-lambda} uniformly over arbitrary N,T,n growth, or whether replication, finite random design, and generated locations produce another term.

source_refs.claim: Repeated-measurement nonparametric regression has a sparse-to-dense minimax phase transition but no separately generated evaluation location.
source_refs.author: Shunxing Yan and Fang Yao

source_refs.claim: Pointwise random-design regression rates depend on local design mass, but the evaluation point and training coordinates are observed.
source_refs.author: Stéphane Gaïffas

source_refs.author: Bruno Ferman
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked construction found the smoothing expression algebraically dominated in its fixed-cohort experiment, while repeated-measurement and pointwise random-design papers analyze observed sites without an independently generated evaluation location. It is therefore unresolved whether the revised sampling architecture creates independent effective sample size Tn, or whether shared sites preserve dominance. The missing proof must simultaneously localize over T random sites, pool n responses per site, and control an N^-1/2 shared location perturbation without cross-terms or logarithmic losses.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matching upper-and-lower minimax theorem over every N,T,n growth array proving the displayed four-term maximum, or an explicit admissible regime and least-favorable subexperiment exhibiting the additional term or dominance relation.

writing_exemplar.why: Its many-period/many-control framing shows why conclusions must be indexed by relative growth rates.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Donors and periods jointly determine synthetic-control behavior -> different growth ratios produce different regimes -> replication and generated locations add competing information channels -> determine the complete N-by-T-by-n frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Use design-adaptive local-polynomial estimation and pointwise alternatives indexed by the realized local design mass.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This isolates the T^-2lambda spacing branch and supplies lower-bound constructions at a realized query.

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose repeated-measurement risk into sparse and dense regimes and match empirical-process upper bounds with packing lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof distinguishes information from within-site replication from information supplied by additional sites.

method_exemplars.technique: Expand a feasible local-polynomial smoother around its oracle counterpart and isolate the first-stage generated-covariate remainder.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired fourth branch is determined by whether the generated-location remainder is exactly N^-lambda.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize when the observable donor-proxy architecture is an exact-center, generated-center, generated-training-coordinate, or classically noisy-training-coordinate experiment, and locate the boundary where oracle equivalence fails or deconvolution becomes unavoidable.

source_refs.excerpt: comparing exact-center, generated-center, and noisy-training-coordinate experiments on the same replicated-site submodel
Cross-fitting alone does not convert either design into a generated-center experiment.

source_refs.claim: Proximal synthetic controls use excluded donor outcomes as proxies but do not derive a generated-proxy minimax phase diagram.
source_refs.author: Xu Shi, Kendrick Li, Wang Miao, Mengtong Hu, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Nonparametric regression on estimated covariates has a leading smoothed first-stage error, but this differs from a center-only perturbation.
source_refs.author: Enno Mammen, Christoph Rothe, and Melanie Schienle

source_refs.claim: Replicated error-prone covariates can recover known-error first-order behavior through deconvolution, within a classical errors-in-variables experiment.
source_refs.author: Aurore Delaigle, Peter Hall, and Alexander Meister

open_problems.why_unsolved: A donor mean used only as the realized evaluation center creates a shared Hölder displacement; estimated coordinates in every training row move smoothing neighborhoods; noisy latent coordinates instead create a convolution inverse problem. These have different likelihood factorizations and rates, yet cross-fitting is sometimes invoked as if it erased the distinction. Neither proximal synthetic-control theory nor generated-regressor theory compares all four observation experiments or decides when replication prevents a deconvolution penalty.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An experiment-comparison or sigma-field characterization assigning each proxy architecture its sharp conditional MSE and honest-length rate, with necessary and sufficient oracle-equivalence inequalities and an explicit least-favorable submodel whenever deconvolution is unavoidable.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames donors as causal proxies and exposes the assumptions under which they identify a counterfactual.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Imperfect pre-treatment fit limits conventional synthetic controls -> excluded donors can act as proxies -> empirical proxy coordinates may themselves be learned -> identify the exact oracle/generated/noisy boundary

method_exemplars.technique: Identify the untreated counterfactual through donor-proxy bridge or moment restrictions conditional on treatment timing.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the causal identification layer whose observation architecture must be classified.

method_exemplars.technique: Use a generated-regressor stochastic expansion to identify terms caused by moving every training coordinate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest benchmark for separating training-coordinate generation from center-only generation.

method_exemplars.technique: Factor the replicated-measurement likelihood, estimate the error law, and analyze the resulting deconvolution estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the adverse inverse-problem branch if donor observations are noisy replicas of latent training coordinates.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a feasible inverse-full-covariance estimator and conditionally honest interval that attain the sharp causal-wealth MSE and square-root expected-length frontier under unknown heteroskedastic donor laws and overlapping geometrically beta-mixing calendar windows.

source_refs.excerpt: add pretreatment covariance estimation under primitive published error conditions
prove that the robustified nested-support program preserves honesty and the frontier comparison.

source_refs.claim: Optimal honest intervals over convex smoothness classes are governed by a modulus under fixed regressors and Gaussian known-variance errors.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong and Michal Kolesár

source_refs.claim: Synthetic-control intervals separate construction and post-treatment uncertainty and allow beta-mixing, but do not optimize expected length with generated proxies.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Yingjie Feng, and Rocío Titiunik
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Covariance-weighted local-linear smoothing can attain linear minimax efficiency when within-cluster correlation is correctly specified.
source_refs.author: Kani Chen, Jianqing Fan, and Zhezhen Jin

source_refs.claim: Spline and wavelet estimators attain optimal rates and functional normality under weak dependence, without a shared generated query path.
source_refs.author: Xiaohong Chen and Timothy M. Christensen

open_problems.why_unsolved: Known-covariance local smoothing and weak-dependence sieve theory do not cover weights whose Mahalanobis neighborhoods, bandwidths, and studentization all use an estimated inverse donor-path covariance. Overlapping windows also prevent naive fold independence. The unresolved perturbation step must show that covariance and long-run-variance estimation errors are negligible relative to every active N,T,n_s branch, while preserving the two-sided modulus and conditional coverage without undersmoothing or logarithmic inflation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A cross-fitted local-polynomial or tensor-sieve estimator with a uniform oracle-equivalence expansion, a calendar-block limit theorem, and a conditionally honest interval whose worst-case expected length matches the square root of the joint minimax risk, accompanied by matching modulus lower bounds.

writing_exemplar.why: Its decomposition of synthetic-control prediction uncertainty provides the closest causal-panel motivation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Synthetic-control estimates are counterfactual predictions -> construction and post-event shocks both generate uncertainty -> reused calendar observations require covariance-aware inference -> generated paths require an honest joint frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Construct an inverse-within-cluster-covariance local-linear smoother and derive its bias-variance and minimax-efficiency expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired estimator is its generated-path, beta-mixing, feasible-covariance analogue.

method_exemplars.technique: Control dependent sieve Gram matrices by random-matrix inequalities and linearize irregular sieve functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A tensor-sieve implementation needs precisely this weak-dependence Gram-matrix and functional-normality machinery.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert the bias-standard-deviation tradeoff encoded by an ordered modulus to construct honest intervals and expected-length lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested interval and lower bound are both governed by the covariance-standardized local modulus.

open_problems.open_problem: Lift the generated-donor fixed-query experiment to an admissible joint causal panel-law class that identifies buy-and-hold level wealth, supplies a genuine FWL representation, and explains why mean-only donor matching fails under volatility drag.

source_refs.excerpt: Lift the treated, spacing, and donor two-point constructions to explicit joint panel-law submodels
it supplies neither an assignment/regression specification nor the required panel regression/FWL representation

source_refs.claim: Causal synthetic-control event studies cover linear cumulative effects but isolate BHAR as difficult because counterfactual portfolios must match volatility.
source_refs.author: Paul Goldsmith-Pinkham and Tianshu Lyu

source_refs.claim: Buy-and-hold abnormal-return tests exhibit benchmark, skewness, new-listing, and rebalancing distortions.
source_refs.author: Brad M. Barber and John D. Lyon

source_refs.claim: Conventional long-run buy-and-hold inference can overreject when overlapping event firms have correlated abnormal returns.
source_refs.author: Mark L. Mitchell and Erik Stafford

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked rate proof is formulated over a union of fixed-query conditional experiments, and its lower-bound witnesses were not shown to arise as regular conditional laws from one joint panel model on positive-probability query sets. Separately, cumulative-return causal event-study theory does not extend automatically to compounded wealth: expected wealth depends on the joint counterfactual return path, so equality of conditional means or factor loadings need not neutralize volatility drag. Assignment structure, path-law correspondence, and the FWL/DID reductions may constrain the cusp, spacing, and donor perturbations used by the statistical lower bounds.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint-panel identifying functional and FWL representation for causal level wealth, an explicit mean-matched counterexample driven by covariance mismatch, and admissible joint-law submodels supporting every minimax lower-bound channel, including T=2 DID and homogeneous-panel reductions.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly contrasts linear event-study targets with geometric buy-and-hold wealth and identifies volatility mismatch as the obstacle.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Traditional financial event studies use fragile factor benchmarks -> synthetic portfolios improve causal counterfactual construction -> compounded wealth also depends on the return-path covariance -> build a joint-law causal panel theory

method_exemplars.technique: Use excluded donor outcomes as proxies and identify untreated counterfactuals through proximal moment restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a donor-proxy identification route that can be strengthened from scalar outcomes to the wealth path law.

method_exemplars.technique: Formalize financial event-study causal estimands and derive misspecification bias for factor-model and synthetic-portfolio counterfactuals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its geometric-return discussion identifies the exact mean-based proof step that breaks for level wealth.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent panel prediction error through primitive reused-cell coefficients and separate construction from post-treatment uncertainty.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the closest route from a joint panel representation to covariance-aware inference for a realized counterfactual path.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive the covariance-standardized two-sided local modulus from primitive donor and regression laws on positive-probability realized-path sets, or characterize precisely when only a one-sided Hölder upper modulus is available.

source_refs.excerpt: The worked law P_ex establishes only that the attainable-direction restriction is non-vacuous
Add a worked non-affine, nondegenerate data-generating example satisfying the attainable local modulus

open_problems.why_unsolved: The previous converse assumes an attainable least-favorable direction, while its worked law proves only non-vacuity and does not derive that condition from the advertised panel primitives. In dimensions above one, a scalar regression cannot satisfy a lower Hölder inequality in every direction, and covariance whitening changes which directions are statistically least favorable. Consequently the N^-kappa lower branch presently depends on a bespoke richness condition rather than a characterized feature of the causal panel class.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient primitive condition producing an attainable ordered local modulus in the donor-covariance Mahalanobis metric on positive-probability path sets, plus an admissible counterexample showing failure of the N^-kappa converse without that condition.

writing_exemplar.why: Its formulation makes the parameter class, ordered modulus, and least-favorable direction explicit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Uniform inference requires a declared function class -> the class induces directional moduli -> covariance selects statistically relevant directions -> derive rather than assume the donor-location modulus

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce the parameter class to hardest chords in the covariance-standardized experiment and characterize attainable target separation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution is exactly a characterization of when the least-favorable chord needed for the donor lower bound exists.

method_exemplars.technique: Separate perturbations of a generated regressor as a conditioning variable from perturbations of its evaluation argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: That decomposition isolates the primitive direction along which a donor-location perturbation changes causal wealth.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend the generated-path frontier to lambda greater than one using local-polynomial or tensor-sieve regression while retaining the saturated donor exponent kappa=min(lambda,1) under moving-center and beta-mixing perturbations.

source_refs.excerpt: REMAINING LIMITATION: higher-order smoothness and exact phase-intersection constants require separate new arguments.
The effective dimension is d=p(H+1) because the stacked path is unrestricted

open_problems.why_unsolved: The previous constructive argument uses nearest-site recovery and is restricted to lambda at most one. For higher-order smoothness, polynomial bias can improve while a root-N generated evaluation path remains first-order regular, suggesting saturation at N^-1. The first proof step that changes is uniform coercivity and perturbation control for a multivariate polynomial Gram matrix centered at an estimated path under dependent realized designs; the earlier Hölder displacement inequality does not establish it.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A conditional upper-and-lower rate theorem for lambda greater than one with dimension d=p(H+1), a feasible cross-fitted local-polynomial or tensor-sieve estimator, a donor term N^-1, and a proof or counterexample deciding whether moving-Gram instability adds a distinct phase.

writing_exemplar.why: Its panel prediction framing keeps the causal destination and temporal dependence central.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Panel counterfactual prediction needs flexible pre-event regression -> higher smoothness promises improved oracle recovery -> the event path is itself generated -> derive the higher-order oracle/generated frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Use multivariate local-polynomial moment matrices, equivalent kernels, and higher-order bias expansions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These are the estimator and proof objects that must replace nearest-site recovery.

method_exemplars.technique: Control weakly dependent sieve Gram matrices and derive asymptotic normality for sieve functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A tensor-sieve alternative must establish stable dependent-design Gram matrices before handling the moving query.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine block coupling with full-covariance conditional prediction after deriving a linear score representation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The higher-order score must remain valid under overlapping beta-mixing calendar windows.

literature_map:
1. Shi, Li, Miao, Hu, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (JASA 2026; arXiv:2108.13935) identify synthetic controls through donor proxies but keep proxy designation predetermined.
2. Qiu et al. (Biometrics 2024; arXiv:2210.02014) give doubly robust proximal-SC formulas and GMM inference, not generated-proxy minimax theory.
3. Park and Tchetgen Tchetgen (Journal of Causal Inference 2025; arXiv:2307.16353) reduce proximal SC to one proxy type and use conformal inference.
4. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (Annals of Statistics 2012; arXiv:1207.5594) provide the key oracle expansion for nonparametrically generated covariates.
5. Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (Annals of Statistics 2008; arXiv:0804.0713) show how replication can recover known-error first-order behavior in deconvolution.
6. Kato and Sasaki (Journal of Econometrics 2019; arXiv:1702.03377) construct uniform bands for errors-in-variables regression using repeated measurements.
7. Gaïffas (ESAIM P&S 2007) establishes pointwise random-design minimax adaptation governed by local design mass.
8. Yan and Yao (arXiv:2302.13908) derive sparse-to-dense phase transitions for repeated-measurement Hölder regression.
9. Chen, Fan, and Jin (Statistica Sinica 2008) show full within-cluster covariance weighting can attain linear minimax efficiency.
10. Chen and Christensen (Journal of Econometrics 2015; arXiv:1412.6020) give optimal weak-dependence sieve rates and irregular-functional normality.
11. Armstrong and Kolesár (Econometrica 2018; arXiv:1511.06028) tie optimal honest expected length to a covariance-standardized modulus.
12. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (JASA 2021; arXiv:1912.07120) split synthetic-control interval uncertainty into construction and post-event components, including beta-mixing.
13. Ferman (JASA 2021; arXiv:1906.06665) demonstrates that synthetic-control validity changes with joint many-period/many-donor growth.
14. Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu (arXiv:2511.15123) leave geometric BHAR outside their linear causal event-study theory because volatility mismatch can create false effects.
15. Barber and Lyon (JFE 1997) and Mitchell and Stafford (Journal of Business 2000) document BHAR benchmark, skewness, overlap, and cross-correlation failures that a causal level-wealth theorem must address.
prior_proposal_map:
1. The banked panel_bhar_proxy_modulus_frontier/proxy_modulus_v1 run was the highest-yield source; its README, proto_core, exact-constant solve packet, and angle0_v1-v3 reviewer JSONs were inspected.
2. Its final general review says the lower-bound witnesses were not lifted from labeled conditional kernels to admissible joint panel laws.
3. Its rubric identifies the missing panel regression/FWL representation and canonical DID reductions.
4. Its README records that replicated-response smoothing was algebraically dominated for fixed cohorts, directly challenging an automatic four-phase claim.
5. angle0_v3 supplies the exact-center/generated-center/noisy-training-coordinate comparison and the deferred phase-intersection program.
6. panel_nested_donor_honest_width_frontier/v1 supplies the unknown-covariance stability and feasible-honesty extension after its known-covariance downgrade.
7. stat_event_surface_extrapolation_minimax/v2 and panel_mnar_eventtime_uniform_band/v1 were inspected for covariance-aware adaptation and growing-band proof boundaries; both reinforce that feasible score and covariance control is not automatic.
8. No proto_core_angle*_rejected.json or legacy rejected-angle proposal was present in the closest BHAR, nested-donor, or event-surface runs.
